draft.title: Sole traders and partnerships
card: An unincorporated business is not a legal entity separate from its owners. In law, the owners and the business are treated as the same.
a business with one owner, who makes the decisions and keeps all the profit. A sole trader can still employ staff.
a business with two or more owners, called partners. They share the work, decisions and profits, often set out in a written partnership agreement.
Both are easy and cheap to start, with little paperwork. But the owners have unlimited liability: if the business cannot pay its debts, they can lose personal assets such as savings, a car or a home.
draft.remember: No separate legal entity means the owners' own assets are on the line for the business's debts.

a.q: Sam runs a plumbing business as a sole trader. It owes $40,000 it cannot pay. What can happen?
opts: Sam may have to sell his own car to pay the debt
Only the business's tools can be sold to pay the debt
The debt is cancelled once the business closes
Sam can lose only the money he put into the business
a.why: A sole trader has unlimited liability, so Sam's personal assets can be used to pay the business's debts. Losing only what he put in would be limited liability, which a sole trader does not have.
a.clue: In law, is Sam separate from his business?

b.q: Ava and Josh run a landscaping partnership in Geelong. It closes owing debts that its assets cannot cover. What is true?
opts: Ava and Josh may have to pay from their own savings
Only the business's assets can be used to pay the debts
The partnership pays alone, as it is separate from them
Their debts are halved because there are two owners
b.why: A partnership is unincorporated, so the partners have unlimited liability and their personal assets can be taken. The tempting idea that the business is a separate legal entity is wrong: an unincorporated business and its owners are the same in law.
b.clue: Think about what unincorporated means for the owners.

a.best: Sam may have to sell his own car to pay the debt

b.best: Ava and Josh may have to pay from their own savings
